summary:
## BoxMOT v26.0.0

BoxMOT v26.0.0 adds multimodal tracking, optional EdgeTAM mask guidance, typed tracker configuration, and joint motion-model selection. It also improves evaluation reproducibility, replay performance, and tuning diagnostics.

Based on committed changes since `v25.0.0`, through `9da023fd`.

### New features and improvements

- **EagerMOT sensor fusion:** Track objects using calibrated 2D and 3D detections, with optional camera poses. New spatial structures represent 3D boxes, camera calibration, and multimodal outputs. Includes KITTI evaluation, class-specific tuning, and 3D Kalman calibration.
- **MAF-HDA mask tracking:** Adds a Python tracker combining motion with mask-based correlation-filter appearance. Supports AABB detections with instance masks without requiring ReID weights.
- **EdgeTAM integration:** Generate detection masks with the standalone segmentor or enable temporal mask-guided association using `--edgetam`. Guidance supports the nine Python box trackers with AABB geometry, IoU association, and `per_class=False`.
- **Typed configuration and simpler factories:** All eleven trackers expose immutable, validated configuration classes with editor completion. Detector, ReID, and tracker factories support simpler construction, while shared `KalmanConfig` and `ReIDConfig` group component settings.
- **Joint motion selection:** `tune --select-kf` compares compatible Kalman filters and noise profiles using held-out predictions. Add `--select-cmc` to jointly select camera-motion compensation. Selected profiles are saved for reuse.
- **More targeted tuning:** Conditional search spaces account for geometry, association metric, and enabled features. New controls expose motion, detection-confidence, and ReID–IoU fusion, with improved trial comparisons and parameter diagnostics.
- **Expanded evaluation:** Adds KITTI-MOTS mask evaluation, saved 2D detection workflows, 3D tracking metrics, and optional official KITTI AP40 reports. Materialized AABB evaluation supports ordered GTA, GSI, and GBRC postprocessing while preserving raw results.
- **Faster repeated workloads:** Batched Kalman operations, optimized camera-motion compensation, indexed embedding reads, reusable workers, and optional `--cache-inputs` reduce repeated processing.
- **Reliability fixes:** Restores per-sequence evaluation reporting, corrects DeepOC-SORT covariance handling during camera compensation, cleans up orphaned workers, and fixes Python 3.10 typing compatibility. OpenCV is pinned to `4.11.0.86`, and its runtime version participates in perception-cache identity.

### Breaking changes

This major release includes breaking changes. When upgrading from v25:

- **Update direct tracker construction.** Pass algorithm settings through the matching config, such as `BotSort(config=BotSortConfig(...))`. The factory also accepts algorithm keywords: `create_tracker("botsort", match_thresh=0.8)`.
- **Group component settings.** Move flat Kalman options into `kalman` and `kalman.noise`; configure tracker-owned appearance through `reid=ReIDConfig(...)` or an injected appearance encoder.
- **Replace `track_buffer`.** ByteTrack and BoT-SORT now use `max_lost_frames`, counted directly in tracker updates without FPS scaling.
- **Review removed tracker features.** SAM2MOT has been removed; standalone SAM segmentation remains available. OccluBoost's online GTA controls are removed, and its AABB/OBB thresholds and lifetime settings are consolidated.
- **Review centroid thresholds.** `centroid_max_distance` now determines geometric eligibility across matching and recovery; overlap thresholds no longer restrict centroid matching.
- **Update commands and imports.** Replace `boxmot time-variant` with `boxmot materialize --time-variant`. Internal tracker and motion modules have moved; prefer public imports from `boxmot`.
- **Rebuild native libraries.** ByteTrack, BoT-SORT, and OccluBoost use constructor ABI v3. Their shared update/result ABI remains v2.
- **Install optional dependencies explicitly.** Use `boxmot install --extra ...`; first-use automatic installation has been removed. Published Docker images are now CPU-only, while GPU build targets remain available.

EdgeTAM currently requires its full PyTorch checkpoint. The registered `export-edgetam` command and TFLite bundle runtime remain unfinished.

summary:
## 🌟 Summary
Release **v8.4.191** improves RKNN INT8 exports, especially for tasks beyond detection, and includes performance and tracking fixes plus Platform documentation updates.

## 📊 Key Changes
- **RKNN INT8 export — main update:** INT8 export is now enabled for detection, segmentation, pose, and oriented bounding box (OBB) models. The NPU runs the head’s output convolutions, while a new `tail.onnx` file runs the box decoding on the CPU in floating point. FP16-capable targets also use RKNN’s `auto_hybrid` option to retain high-error layers in floating point.
- **RKNN deployment notes:** The decode tail requires ONNX Runtime, which Ultralytics installs automatically when needed. Custom runtimes must run `tail.onnx` or implement the same decoding. Re-export INT8 models made with earlier versions to avoid incorrect coordinate scaling. INT8 accuracy has been tested in the RKNN simulator, but not yet validated on Rockchip hardware.
- **Faster segmentation training:** Finds foreground anchors across the batch in one pass instead of repeating work per image. Losses and gradients remain unchanged; the reported Tesla T4 timings show modest training-step improvements.
- **More efficient parking management:** Computes each tracked car’s center once per frame rather than once for every parking-space comparison, reducing repeated work.
- **Improved OC-SORT matching:** Measures detection direction over the track’s recent `delta_t`-frame window, making associations less sensitive to box jitter.
- **Preserved prediction-manifest order:** Images and videos listed in TXT or CSV sources are now processed in the order provided, rather than being reordered alphabetically.
- **Platform and guide updates:** Platform documentation now includes MiniMax as an annotation provider, explains saved Roboflow and W&B import keys and OBB labels in detection datasets, and features an updated YOLO26 batch-processing video.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- The RKNN change targets the accuracy loss caused by running box decoding in INT8 on the NPU. Keeping that decode on the CPU in floating point is intended to improve accuracy and broaden INT8 support across vision tasks.
- The training and parking-management changes reduce unnecessary repeated work without changing the described outputs, while the OC-SORT fix may help maintain more reliable tracking when detections are jittery.
- Manifest ordering now better matches the sequence users explicitly specify—useful, for example, when listing video frames in playback order.

## What's Changed
* Platform docs: add MiniMax to the paid annotation vendors by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26902
* Find segment loss foreground anchors once per batch by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26914
* Compute ParkingManagement car centers once per frame by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26910
* Update batch processing video in Model Training Tips guide by @RizwanMunawar in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26908
* Align Platform docs with saved import keys and OBB labels in detect datasets by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26906
* Measure OC-SORT OCM detection direction over delta_t frames by @mottopanikeiku in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26912
* Keep the listed order of sources in TXT and CSV prediction manifests by @MohammadHijjawi97 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26903
* `ultralytics 8.4.191` Fix RKNN INT8 accuracy with a host-side decode tail for all tasks by @Bovey0809 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26904


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.190...v8.4.191
